beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude UI, ask shown answered
beats.narration_text: Mohammed Hussain. I build with Claude, then I take it apart to see if it holds up. The ask: run a private, chat-with-your-data system with zero calls to any outside API. Two free tools do it — Ollama for inference, Open WebUI for the interface — plus retrieval-augmented generation to ground answers in your own documents. Let's build it.

props.command: how do I run a private, on-prem "chat with your data" system with zero third-party API calls?
output: Ollama — local model runtime, REST API on :11434
Open WebUI — chat frontend, talks ONLY to Ollama
RAG — retrieval, not retraining, grounds every answer
0 API keys anywhere in this stack

beats.role_note: stakes — BEFORE the CLI loop, no composer yet; SHOW-DON'T-TELL: animated boundary diagram
beats.narration_text: Chat-with-your-data usually means uploading documents to somebody else's API — HR files, contracts, product specs, leaving the building on every question. For plenty of orgs that's a non-starter: compliance, client agreements, plain risk aversion. The fix isn't a smarter model. It's a smaller network — inference and retrieval both running on hardware you already control, so the question never has anywhere to travel.
beats.visual_intent: A document icon flies right toward a box labeled THIRD-PARTY API and is stopped by a red X halfway — that path is cut. The same document icon then loops entirely inside a box labeled YOUR HARDWARE, passing through an OLLAMA node and back, closing on a green check labeled '0 external calls.' No composer in this beat.

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — show and discuss the prompt; SPARK-LINE: 'The ask,'
beats.narration_text: The ask names the one thing that actually keeps this private: OLLAMA_BASE_URL has to point inside the Docker network, at the Ollama container by name — never at an external host. Get that one environment variable right and nothing ever leaves the machine; get it wrong and you've quietly wired in a cloud dependency.

props.command:
claude "write a docker-compose.yml that runs Ollama + Open WebUI
  together. Open WebUI's OLLAMA_BASE_URL must point at Ollama's
  OWN container over the internal Docker network — never an
  external host. Expose Open WebUI on 3000, Ollama on 11434,
  persist both with named volumes."

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — THE ACTUAL-CODE LAW: real compose file, trimmed to teaching lines
beats.narration_text: Read the environment line: OLLAMA_BASE_URL set to Ollama's own container name on port eleven-four-three-four. That's not a placeholder — it's Docker's internal network resolving one service to another, the same way any two containers in one compose file find each other. Open WebUI never learns an external URL exists. Two named volumes keep the model weights and chat history on disk across restarts.

props.title: docker-compose.yml
props.code:
services:
  ollama:
    image: ollama/ollama:latest
    ports: ["11434:11434"]
    volumes: ["ollama-data:/root/.ollama"]

  open-webui:
    image: ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main
    ports: ["3000:8080"]
    environment:
      - OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://ollama:11434   # ← the whole trick
    volumes: ["open-webui-data:/app/backend/data"]
    depends_on: [ollama]

volumes:
  ollama-data:
  open-webui-data:
props.sparkLine: One env var keeps it private.

beats.role_note: bonus mechanism beat — Part 1 hardware table, redrawn as bars (simplified, RAM-only)
beats.narration_text: Before you pull a model, size the hardware honestly. An 8B model like Llama 3.1 wants eight to sixteen gigs of RAM — slow, but it runs on CPU alone. Qwen3-30B-A3B, a mixture-of-experts model, activates only about three billion parameters per token: answers bigger than it is, fits in sixteen to twenty-four gigs. A 70B-class model needs a real GPU. Embedding models stay tiny regardless — don't over-provision for that half.
beats.visual_intent: Three horizontal bars grow left to right: '8B model' to 8–16GB (green, CPU-OK label); 'Qwen3-30B-A3B (MoE, ~3B active)' to 16–24GB (amber, GPU-recommended label); '70B-class' to 40–48GB+ (red, GPU-required label). A small footnote bar: 'embedding models: ~100–600M params — CPU always fine.' Caption, small: 'Redrawn (simplified) from the source's Part 1 hardware table.'

beats.role_note: moving visualization, never a still — the RAG pipeline running WITHOUT an embedding model wired
beats.narration_text: docker compose up, pull the 8B model, ask it about the HR handbook. Watch the pipeline: the handbook never got chunked or embedded — no embedding model is configured yet — so nothing retrieves. The model answers anyway, confidently, straight from its own training. Zero chunks retrieved, and it just invented a policy that isn't in the handbook at all.
beats.visual_intent: A document icon 'HR-handbook.pdf' sits static and greyed out, labeled NOT EMBEDDED — no chunk split, no vectors. A question bubble arrives and searches; no line draws to anything. A red badge flashes '0 chunks retrieved.' An answer bubble appears anyway with a warning tag: 'fabricated — not in source.'

beats.narration_text: The tell was the confidence — a fluent answer that cited nothing. That's not a model problem, it's a wiring problem: no embedding model means no vectors means no retrieval. The fix pulls nomic-embed-text, sets it as the RAG embedder in Open WebUI's Documents settings, and checks chunk size — five hundred to a thousand tokens, the range that keeps a chunk coherent without diluting it.

props.command:
claude "the RAG answer above cites nothing — that's a hallucination,
  not a retrieval. Pull the nomic-embed-text embedding model in
  Ollama, set it as Open WebUI's RAG embedder (Admin Panel →
  Settings → Documents), and re-check retrieval on the same
  question. Also tighten chunk size to 500–1000 tokens."

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the actual fix: real pull command + real settings, not prose
beats.narration_text: Two commands, one settings screen. Pull the embedding model the same way you pulled the LLM. Point Open WebUI's Documents settings at it. Re-upload the knowledge collection so every chunk actually gets vectorized this time — nothing before this step had a vector to search, which is the entire reason the first answer had nothing to retrieve.

props.title: fix: wire the embedder
props.code:
# 1. pull the embedding model into Ollama
docker exec -it ollama ollama pull nomic-embed-text

# 2. Open WebUI → Admin Panel → Settings → Documents
#    Embedding Engine:  Ollama
#    Embedding Model:   nomic-embed-text
#    Chunk Size:        750
#    Chunk Overlap:     100

# 3. re-upload the Knowledge collection so it re-embeds
#    with the now-configured model

beats.role_note: moving visualization — the SAME pipeline, now grounded; THE REVISION LAW satisfied
beats.narration_text: Same question, re-run. The handbook is now chunks, each chunk a vector in ChromaDB. The question embeds too, the system finds the three closest chunks, and hands them to the model as context. The answer comes back citing the actual policy line — three chunks retrieved, grounded, no invention. The model didn't get smarter. The pipeline finally had something to search.
beats.visual_intent: The handbook splits into chunk rectangles that fly into a ChromaDB cluster as dots (vectors). A question bubble arrives, embeds, and draws lines to the 3 nearest dots (highlighted). Those 3 chunks fly into the model's context-window box. An answer bubble emerges tagged 'Source: HR Handbook §4.2.' A green badge reads '3 chunks retrieved.'

beats.role_note: ClaudeVerdictArtifact — the lesson in one beat
beats.narration_text: What this build actually proved: privacy here is one environment variable, not a philosophy. RAG works by retrieval, not memorization — which means a missing embedding model doesn't degrade an answer, it deletes retrieval entirely. And chunk size, not model size, was the lever that turned a hallucination into a grounded, citable answer.

props.artifactTitle: Chat With Your Own Data, Zero API Calls
artifactLines: OLLAMA_BASE_URL pointed inward is the entire privacy boundary.
RAG grounds answers by retrieval, not by retraining the model.
No embedding model configured means zero chunks retrieved — not a smaller error.
Chunk size, not model size, was the lever that fixed the answer.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — prompt READ aloud and discussed; greeting 'Your turn.'
beats.narration_text: Your turn. That prompt hands Claude your actual hardware and your actual documents and asks for the compose file, the embedding model, a starting chunk size, and a way to verify nothing calls out — the same four decisions this build just walked through, sized to what you've actually got. Run the stack, watch the retrieval count on your first real question, and fix the wiring, not the model, when it comes back empty.
